methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Nyobolt is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Sai Shivareddy and Clare Grey, having raised over $100M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company (LNZA) operating in advanced battery, materials, and hydrogen sectors at Series B–C stages, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $100M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B step-ups, implying $190M. Peer-median analysis compares Nyobolt to three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median of this peer set is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B. This substantial peer dispersion reflects heterogeneous technology risk and investor conviction within frontier energy.

Triangulating these methods yields a valuation range of $162M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $595M. Stage-progression anchors the lower bound; peer comparables drive significant upside, though wide peer dispersion ($700M–$3.0B) introduces material uncertainty around appropriate valuation multiples for pre-revenue deep-tech. Key uncertainties include technology validation progress, capital intensity to commercialization, and investor appetite for extended pre-revenue timelines in climate hardware.
